chunks: O Allah! Whoever of Your servants hears our utterance which is just and not deviant,
and after hearing it refuses nothing but to turn away from supporting You, and to delay in strengthening Your religion,
then we call You to witness against him, O Greatest of Witnesses, with a testimony, and we call all whom You have settled on Your earth and in Your skies to witness against him,
then You alone are the One who makes us needless of his support, and the One who takes him to account for his sin.
ai.seo_question: What does the supplication in Nahj al-Balagha say about those who reject the call to support the righteous cause?
ai.summary: This supplication, often cited in the context of the Khawarij or those who abandoned Imam Ali during the Battle of Siffin, emphasizes the obligation of *Nasr* (support) for the righteous leader. It invokes Allah and all of creation as witnesses against those who hear the truth yet choose negligence (*Nukus*), thereby transferring the burden of accountability solely to Allah. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on the political and spiritual necessity of standing with the Imam to preserve the integrity of the religion.
